episodes.211360: An upper level trough and low level trough to the northwest of Hawaii brought numerous flooding impacts. These flooding impacts closed roads and damaged property across the state.
episodes.211367: A series of minor weather disturbances moved through the region from April 9th through the 11th. These combined with increased moisture to bring showers and storms to the region. With enough wind shear available in the atmosphere, some of these storms brought severe wind gusts to the region.  Dry and windy conditions were in place on April 9th and that helped drive the spread of a wildfire known as Mary 15 to almost 900 acres.  Additionally, the Lightning Roll Wildfire would be sparked due to dry lightning in Beaver County on the evening of April 9th.  That fire would go on to burn 2,412 acres.
episodes.211368: A series of minor weather disturbances moved through the region from April 9th through the 11th. These combined with increased moisture to bring showers and storms to the region. With enough wind shear available in the atmosphere, some of these storms brought severe wind gusts to the region. Dry and windy conditions were in place on April 9th and that helped drive the spread of a wildfire known as The Smooth Eddy Incident which was over 500 acres. Additionally, the Purple Monster Wildfire would be sparked due to dry lightning in Oldham County on the evening of April 9th. That fire would go on to burn 1,911 acres.
episodes.211653: During the late afternoon hours of April 9th, storms brought damaging wind gusts to Leavenworth County KS.
episodes.211795: A spring storm brought rain, mountain snow and thunderstorms to interior northern California in early to mid April. Gusty winds with a line of thunderstorms on April 11th between 5:00 PM and 9:00 PM led to numerous reports of tree damage and power outages in the Greater Sacramento Area and into the adjacent Sierra foothills, with measured wind gusts of 35 to 40 mph observed. There were also numerous reports of roadway flooding. A touchdown of an EF-U tornado occurred from 2:05 PM to 2:06 PM on April 12th near Vina, CA. There were also reports of severe hail in thunderstorms. Heavy mountain snow brought major travel impacts to the Sierra Nevada from April 10th through 12th. UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab measured 42.6 inches of heavy snow. Kirkwood Ski Resort measured 41 inches of heavy snow. Wind gusts in the Sierra were measured generally between 45 and 55 mph.
episodes.211866: Clusters of severe storms developed across north central Kansas in the early evening before tracking southeast into the late evening hours towards portions of northeast Kansas. Storms produced large hail up to hen egg size (2 inches), wind damage to a barn and trees, and heavy rainfall up to 5 inches in Marshall county.
episodes.211937: An area of showers and thunderstorms that had developed along a quasi-stationary front over southern Kansas, moved slowly southward across much of northeastern Oklahoma during the morning and afternoon of the 10th. Locally heavy rainfall amounts of two to three inches in just a few hours occurred across portions of northeastern Oklahoma, which resulted in isolated flash flooding.
episodes.212487: During the late afternoon and evening hours of April 9th, 2026, a surface boundary draped over northeast Kansas into north-central Missouri retreated northward. As the boundary moved north, moisture pooled across the far southern portions of the area, pushing dew points into the low 50s. A shortwave moved over the southern half of the region, and combined with continued low-level warm advection, triggered an area of thunderstorms along the boundary through the late afternoon and evening.||Deep-layer wind shear (0-6 km bulk shear) of 40 to 50 knots combined with most unstable CAPE (MUCAPE) of 500 to 1,000 J/kg fostered an environment capable of supporting severe convection. As these severe storms tracked eastward into southwest Iowa, they produced damaging wind gusts. A 59 mph wind gust was measured in Mills County, followed by a 58 mph wind gust in Page County between 6 and 7 PM CST.
episodes.213041: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of central Kansas during the afternoon and evening hours of April 9th. Large hail up to golf ball size were reported.
